How we work

Start with one floor. Scale what works.

01

Site walk

We visit, look at your cameras, drawings and bills, and agree on the problem worth solving first.

02

Pilot

A working system on one floor, building or plant room, measured against your real numbers.

03

Roll out

Extend to the whole site once the pilot has proven itself, with your team trained along the way.

04

Support

Monitoring, fixes and a regular report of what the system caught and what it saved.

Featured build · EnergyCam

The room emptied. The AC didn’t notice.

EnergyCam is our first product in the field. It reads the CCTV stream, counts people with YOLOv8, checks each AC, and emails the facilities team a snapshot when cooling runs in an empty room. When someone returns or the AC goes off, a second email closes the alert.

  • Two ACs per room, tracked separately, with readings smoothed over four frames.
  • One alert per event, then a “resolved” email with how long the waste lasted.
  • A live dashboard with a cost ticker in rupees, month-on-month waste and CO2 impact.

FAQ

Questions facility teams ask us.

Do we need to buy new hardware?

Usually not to start. EnergyCam runs on your existing IP cameras, digital twins start from your drawings, and the quotation agent works from email. We tell you up front if anything extra is needed.

How does a project start?

With a short site walk and a conversation about what costs you most. Then we run a small pilot on one floor, one building or one plant room, so you see results before rolling it out.

How is pricing worked out?

Every building is different, so we scope each project after the site walk and send you a clear quote.

Where do you work?

We are based in Karachi and work with buildings across Pakistan. Message us on WhatsApp to talk about your site.

Who is behind Mimar AI?

Mimar AI was founded by Shamroze Nasir, a facility engineer who spent years running buildings. Everything we build comes from problems he saw on site.

Tell us about your building.

Send a message with your building type and the problem that costs you most. We’ll suggest where to start.
